text:
incident-bot: PROD ALERT: sharp p99 tail latency spike on /v1/streaming/generate (continuous-batching path) in prod-usw2. p95: 420ms -> 1.2s, p99: 3.8s -> 9.5s. Streaming stalls reported by customers. Paging eng-oncall. docs: https://dashboards.redwood/streams/prod-usw2
Alex G: taking pager, jumping in now. any immediate customer reports?
Lena R: CSM flagged 2 high-touch customers seeing partial streams/timeouts. I can draft a short note once we know mitigation.
Mira T: I'm checking worker pool metrics and KV cache hit rates. Initial glance: a small subset of workers show sustained large batch sizes (30-60) and their CPU/GPU utilization is fine but end-to-end latency for streaming tokens is increasing.
Sanjay P: suspected mixed-seqlen problem — a few long sequences are getting into continuous batches and inflating completion time for the streaming path. Seen this before with `kb-batcher` (continuous streaming batcher).
Alex G: can we quickly reduce max batch size or bias scheduler fairness to short-seq tasks? want something with low blast radius.
Mira T: two low-risk knobs we can flip:
- set CONT_BATCHER_MAX_BATCH=8 for the streaming pool (runtime API)
- temporarily bump scheduler short-task weight to 3x to prefer small seqs
I can apply the batch cap first, then adjust scheduler if needed.
Ryan K: if you flip the batch size it will increase throughput cost but should improve tail latency. ok from my side.
Mira T: executing runtime patch now:
```bash
# runtime API - patch streaming pool config
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN' https://ops-api.redwood/internal/pools/prod-usw2/streaming/config -d '{"continuous_batcher_max_batch":8}'
```
pagerduty-bot: user alex_g acknowledged the pager.
Mira T: patch accepted, rolling to 20% of streaming workers (canary). watching metrics.
(10m) Mira T: canary shows p99 drop from 9.5s -> 2.1s on canary workers, p95 down to 600ms. Overall cluster p99 starting to trend down.
Sanjay P: good sign. still curious why so many large batches formed — digging into request traces for sequence length distribution.
Alex G: can you dump a sample of request headers from the affected workers? need sequence lengths and client ids.
Sanjay P: pulling traces now, sample output:
```
trace_id: 0xabc123, client: customer-42, seq_len: 1024, arrival_ts: 2165431887
trace_id: 0xabc456, client: unknown, seq_len: 980, arrival_ts: 2165431890
trace_id: 0xabc789, client: customer-7, seq_len: 18, arrival_ts: 2165431892
```
Sanjay P: looks like a handful of very long requests (900-1200 tokens) overlapped with many short ones, causing the batcher to wait/accumulate. continuous batcher currently tries to fill to target size which hurt streaming tail.
Lena R: CSMs want ETA for mitigation and whether to reach customers.
Alex G: mitigation ETA ~10-15m for global roll after canary. recommend holding customer comms until we confirm global leveling.
Mira T: scheduling weight change queued next. applying scheduler change to bias short tasks (non-disruptive):
```yaml
# scheduler-config patch
patch: |
  - op: replace
    path: /pools/streaming/scheduler/short_task_weight
    value: 3
```
Mira T: scheduler patch applied -> rolling.
(25m) Mira T: cluster-wide metrics show p99 at 1.1s (steady), p95 480ms. streaming stall incidents dropping to 0/min.
Alex G: nice. logging a temporary mitigation: max_batch=8 + short-task weight=3. will follow up with more durable fix (batcher timeouts + per-client circuit breaker).
Sanjay P: I’ll open an investigation ticket for root cause: why long sequences are funneled into this pool (routing policies) and add a test for mixed seqlen degradation.
Lena R: CSM update drafted: "We observed transient streaming latency spikes affecting a small number of customers. We've applied a configuration change that restored latency to expected levels and are investigating root cause. We'll follow up with a technical postmortem and any recommended client-side mitigations." Want me to send?
Alex G: send now to the two affected CSMs. include brief guidance: retry/backoff and reduce max tokens if possible while we investigate.
Ryan K: ops note — we should avoid changing batching defaults without a gradual rollout next time. consider adding an automated canary gate that measures p99 before global roll.
Mira T: agreed, adding a gating check to rollout pipeline. filing PR now.
(45m) Mira T: monitoring for 20m window before marking incident resolved. no new regressions.
Alex G: handing off to Mira for the overnight watch. key items for handoff:
- current mitigations: continuous_batcher_max_batch=8, short_task_weight=3
- followups: scheduler fairness audit, routing policy check, runbook update to include this mitigation path, add canary gate PR #4582
- customers notified by CSMs (Lena)
Mira T: ack handoff, I’ll monitor and escalate if p99 climbs >1.5s.
Alex G: thanks everyone.
pagerduty-bot: incident annotated and closed (status: mitigated) — incident ID INC-21654321. Reopen if p99 > 1.5s for more than 5m.
(1h) incident-bot: follow-up note: mitigation succeeded, creating postmortem ticket and adding runbook section "Streaming path: continuous-batcher tail mitigation". next steps assigned to Sanjay (root cause), Mira (runbook+canary gate), Alex (postmortem owner).
Mira T: quick note for postmortem: capture the request routing snapshot, per-client seqlen histogram, and timeline of config changes.
Sanjay P: on it — will attach traces and a replay test.
Lena R: customers acknowledged the update, no escalations.
Alex G: closing thread — leave channel if no more alerts.
